posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Here is the announcement of the rule change.

With the old ruling by order cards entered play response triggers and card text were tiggered simultaneously when the card entered play.

Since it was simultaneous the order of resolution was determined by order the cards entered play, which meant the newly played card went last.

 

Now that order is up to the players.  If you want to keep it the old way (my group does) that is your decision.  But if you want you could let the newly played card go first, or even decide each time in the way that will benefit you most.

I understand the need for this ruling, and pushed for it, but I liked the interaction before the rule change, so we've kept it timed that way, now because we want to instead of because it is the proper way to play.

posts.cooked: Similar rulings have been issued with regard to Sudden Shopping Trip and Negative Energy Field.  Resolve the card play fully, then look for triggers.  The OoO ruling shouldn't apply.  I believe it works the same way for powers.  The issue is that sometimes resolving something fully can take an awful long time (true of card plays, and of powers that put a card into play, such as Timeshift).  The stack has to completely clear before anything can happen as a result of the first stacked event...things that happen in response to the second stacked effect will stack themselves in place of that effect as soon as it's cleared.

"Simple" has nothing to due with being "simultaneous"

Multiple effects that change damage type (lets say the +1 vats from Pike Industrial that turn damage Toxic and Ra's Imbued Fire) are absolutely considered simultaneous, so you are very wrong on that count. 

Playing a one shot triggers the effects on the card. There are other effects in the game that trigger upon playing a card. Because they have common triggers, the effects nessesarily are simultaneous.

Does that make sense?

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: If they were "simultaneous", then each one would constantly overwrite the other and the game would freeze.  They must be consecutive, so that one can trump the other.  If you roll them into the OoO ruling, it makes it possible to declare either one as "high trump", which does reduce the bookkeeping of which one was in play first, and that's what the OoO ruling was about).  But they cannot possibly be "simultaneous", any more than two different answers to "Which day of the week is it" can both be correct (given that the answer is the name of a day, and not something cutesy like "Tomorrow" or "hump day").
